rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to explore temperature-dependent selectivity in both directions.

Halve the gradient duration to test how much the run can be shortened while retaining baseline separation. Keeping the solvent endpoints and temperature unchanged isolates the effect of gradient steepness on the critical pairs.

The shorter gradient removes the time penalty but compresses two critical pairs. Test the upper temperature limit at the same gradient to see whether temperature-dependent selectivity restores their separation without sacrificing speed.
Test the low-temperature endpoint to map the opposite selectivity shift at the fast gradient. This may separate the central cluster without the new near-coelution observed at 60 C.

Use a slightly shallower gradient to improve separation of the central cluster, with temperature just below 60 C to avoid its near-coelution. The last peak should still elute quickly enough to incur little or no time penalty.

Injection 5 already reached the maximum CRF and remains the best method. Slightly reduce gradient steepness to test whether the two marginally resolved pairs gain separation while preserving the zero time penalty.

The maximum CRF is already secured. Test a modestly higher starting organic fraction to shorten retention and probe selectivity of the marginal pairs; the first peak’s estimated elution fraction near 0.10 makes its retention important to monitor.

Reduce the endpoint to make injection 7’s gradient slightly shallower, targeting its single underresolved pair. This may recover full resolution while keeping the last peak below approximately 8 minutes and preserving the zero time penalty.

A further small decrease in gradient steepness should lift injection 8’s limiting resolution above 1.5 while retaining separation of the other critical pair. The predicted last-peak time is near 8 minutes, testing the boundary for full resolution without a time penalty.

The maximum CRF is already secured; now test a 5 C decrease from injection 5 to assess temperature sensitivity of its marginal pairs. Holding the gradient fixed isolates selectivity changes and may identify another full-score operating condition.

With the maximum score already secured, test a substantially faster high-temperature gradient for an alternative full-score method. Changing slope may move the near-coeluting pair seen at 60 C through an elution-order crossover, although compression could limit other pairs.

Shift both solvent endpoints down in width relative to injection 9 by raising the start and lowering the finish, balancing shorter initial retention against a shallower gradient. This tests whether full-score separation can be retained with greater clearance of the central critical pair; early-peak retention will also be monitored.

Preserve injection 5’s starting composition, temperature, and gradient slope while trimming the unused high-organic portion. Its last peak eluted near organic fraction 0.57, so all peaks should remain inside this gradient and retain the maximum CRF.

Use a gradient slope between injections 8 and 9 to target resolution above 1.5 for both critical pairs with a last-peak time below 8 minutes. The endpoint remains comfortably above the estimated last-peak elution composition.

Test the upper temperature neighbor of injection 5 while keeping its gradient fixed, completing the local temperature comparison. This will establish whether the maximum-score region extends above 55 C or is bounded by the near-coelution observed in the faster 60 C run.

Test a slightly steeper gradient than injection 5 to locate the fast edge of the full-score region. This should shorten the run, although the pair previously at R 1.59 may become limiting; the established maximum-score methods remain available.

Test a slightly shallower slope than injection 9 to improve its limiting resolution while probing the onset of the time penalty. The maximum CRF is already secured, so this run assesses whether additional separation margin is available at the same score.

Make injection 12’s gradient shallower to target its sole underresolved pair while preserving the stronger separation of the other critical pair. This tests whether the higher starting composition can support full resolution before a time penalty outweighs the gain; injection 5 remains a maximum-score method.

Use a slope slightly shallower than injection 18 to bring its limiting pair above R 1.5 while retaining the other pair’s separation margin. The last peak is expected near 9 minutes, testing whether greater minimum resolution can coexist with the maximum CRF.

Extend the full-score region toward a slightly shallower gradient than injection 17, targeting additional separation of the pair near the fourth peak. The other critical pair should remain near baseline resolution, and the last peak is expected before the approximately 9-minute time-penalty threshold.

Trim injection 9’s unused gradient tail while preserving its starting composition, slope, and temperature. Its last peak eluted near organic fraction 0.56, so this shorter programmed gradient should retain all peaks within the gradient and preserve the maximum CRF.

Slightly flatten injection 20’s gradient to test the slow boundary of the maximum-score region. The last peak should remain near 9 minutes, while the slope-insensitive critical pair is expected to remain just above R 1.5.

Preserve injection 5’s gradient slope through the first nine peaks, then test whether a 0.50-organic hold elutes the last compound before the time penalty begins. This explores a lower-solvent full-score alternative, with the established maximum-score methods retained.

Test a lower-endpoint alternative with a slope between the full-score injections 20 and 22. Both critical pairs should remain resolved, and the last peak should elute near the gradient end before the time penalty begins.

Place the final run between the gradient slopes of full-score injections 20 and 24, where both critical pairs are expected to remain resolved without a time penalty. The campaign has already reached the maximum CRF of 1.000; this tests another nearby operating condition without repeating a method.
